security.title: Security Architecture
security.desc: Your privacy is not a feature — it's the foundation. Here's exactly how we keep your data safe.
security.fact1_desc: All image processing runs in your browser via WebAssembly (WASM). No image bytes ever leave your device.
security.fact2_desc: PDQ hash is a mathematical fingerprint. It is computationally impossible to reconstruct your image from the hash.
security.fact3_desc: All hashes stored in our database are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.3).
security.pdq_p1: We use <0>PDQ (Photo DNA for Quicker detection)</0>, an algorithm developed by Meta and widely deployed by major platforms to detect CSAM and NCII.
security.pdq_p2: PDQ works by converting an image into a 256-bit binary fingerprint based on visual patterns. Two images that look visually identical (even after minor edits like color shifts or slight crops) will produce very similar hashes.
security.pdq_p3: When a platform tries to upload an image, it hashes it using PDQ and compares against our database. If the Hamming distance (similarity score) is below a threshold, the upload is blocked.
security.oss_desc: Our entire codebase is open-source. You or any security researcher can audit exactly what the code does with your images. We publish all security audits publicly.

verify.desc: Don't take our word for it. In 5 minutes, you can independently confirm that your images never leave your device — using your browser's own built-in tools.
verify.how1_d: The file is loaded into your browser's memory — it never leaves your tab.
verify.how2_d: A WebAssembly program runs inside your browser and converts the image into a 64-char code called a PDQ hash.
verify.how3_d: Only that short code is sent to our server. The image itself stays on your device.
verify.doubts_desc: Our code is 100% open source. You can read every line and verify exactly what gets sent to our server.
verify.step1_d: Open your browser's Developer Tools. This is built into every browser — no install needed.
verify.step2_d: At the top of DevTools, click the "Network" tab. This records every request your browser sends to any server.
verify.step3_t: Go to /protect and Select a File
verify.step3_d: Now go to the Protect page, agree to eligibility, and select an image or video. Keep DevTools open and watch what happens.
verify.step4_d: After submitting, you'll see one request to "/api/cases" in the Network tab. Click it and go to the "Payload" or "Request" tab.
verify.step5_d: In the Network tab, look at the "Size" column for the /api/cases request. Compare it with the size of your image file.
verify.step4_proof: The payload contains only a short string of characters — the hash. Your original image file is nowhere in this request.
verify.step5_proof: Congratulations — you have now independently verified that Raksha Hash never sends your images to any server. Only a 64-character text fingerprint is transmitted.
verify.step2_tip: If the Network tab is empty, refresh the page once.
verify.step2_filter: Type "api" in the filter box to see only API calls.
verify.step3_watch: A request to /api/cases — that's the only server call.
verify.step3_notice: No image file appears in the network requests at all.
verify.step4_size: 0 bytes — the actual file is never in the request.
verify.step5_ex: Your image: 3.2 MB → Request sent: ~200 bytes
verify.step5_conc: Only a tiny text hash was sent, never the image.
verify.footer_t: Ready to protect your media securely?
verify.footer_d: Now that you've verified how the platform works, you can safely hash your media files on your device.

about.desc_p1: is India's first free, open-source tool to prevent Non-Consensual Intimate Image (NCII) abuse — also known as "revenge porn."
about.desc_p2: It empowers survivors and potential victims to register a digital fingerprint (hash) of their private images without ever uploading those images to any server. All hashing is done locally on your device.
about.privacy_desc: Your images never leave your phone. Only a 64-char fingerprint is stored.
about.instant_desc: Register your images in under 60 seconds.
about.tech_desc: We use a technology called perceptual hashing (PDQ), originally developed by Meta to detect CSAM. When you upload an image:
about.step1: Your image is processed entirely in your browser.
about.step3: The hash — not the image — is sent to our secure database.
about.step4: Partner platforms check against our database before allowing any upload.
about.builder_desc: Raksha Hash is an open-source project built by privacy advocates and engineers from India who believe every woman deserves digital safety. We are not affiliated with any government body or tech corporation.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.desc: Everything you need to know about Raksha Hash and your privacy.
faq.q0: 📸 Will my photo be uploaded to the server?
faq.a0: Absolutely not. Your photo never leaves your phone or computer. Only a 64-character "code" (fingerprint) is sent to us — like a unique name for your photo. The photo cannot be recreated from this code.
faq.q1: 🔢 What is a hash or fingerprint?
faq.a1: Think of it like an Aadhaar card number — a unique ID that belongs only to your photo. Even if someone crops the photo or changes the color slightly, this ID will still match and the photo will be blocked.
faq.a2: In Saheli Mode, you can add a trusted friend or family member (like a sister, mother, or best friend). They get a private link to see your case status without needing your PIN. If anything happens to you, they can help immediately.
faq.a3: We are working with Indian social media platforms and messaging apps. International platforms like Meta and Twitter have their own NCII programs. Our goal is to enable detection everywhere simultaneously.
faq.a4: Yes, 100% free — forever. No hidden charges, no subscriptions. This is an open-source, non-profit initiative.
faq.q5: ✂️ What if the abuser edits the photo?
faq.a5: Raksha Hash is smart — slight cropping, color changes, or format changes won't bypass detection. However, heavy AI editing (like deepfakes) requires different tools. We update our models continuously.
faq.a6: Yes! Go to the dashboard, enter your Case ID and PIN, and click "Delete Case." All your hashes will be permanently deleted immediately.
faq.q7: 🤖 Are AI-generated or deepfake images accepted?
faq.a7: Yes. If an AI-generated image depicts you in a sexual manner without consent, you can register its hash.
faq.q8: 🔍 Can I verify that the photo wasn't sent?
faq.a8: Absolutely! See our "Verify Yourself" page — there's a step-by-step guide on how to use browser DevTools to check for yourself that only the hash was sent.
faq.q9: ⚖️ How do I take legal action after registering?
faq.a9: Check our "Legal Action Guide" (/legal) page. You can: (1) Report directly to platforms — Cybercrime Portal, Meta, StopNCII (2) Generate a ready-to-use FIR draft in Hindi or English (3) Find emergency helplines — 1930, 7827170170.
faq.q10: 🔑 I forgot my Case ID or PIN. What should I do?
faq.a10: Unfortunately, we cannot help. Because Raksha Hash is end-to-end encrypted, even we don't know your PIN. Please save your Case ID and PIN immediately in a notes app or a password manager.
